cannot find symbol.explanation: The compiler reached a name it does not know. Java has to be told about every name before it is used - by declaring a variable, defining a method, or importing a class.
cannot find symbol.cause: A spelling mistake, a missing import, or using a variable outside the braces it was declared in.

'<token>' expected.explanation: Java expected a particular character at that spot and found something else. The compiler's own message names the character it wanted - a semicolon, a bracket, a brace or a comma.
'<token>' expected.cause: A forgotten semicolon or an unclosed bracket - usually at the end of the line BEFORE the one the compiler names.

illegal start of expression.explanation: Java found something in a place where a value was expected and cannot make sense of it.
illegal start of expression.cause: An unclosed brace earlier in the file, or a method defined inside another method.
illegal start of expression.example:
int x = ;      // nothing to assign
int x = 0;

class, interface, enum, or record expect.explanation: At the top level of a Java file, only class, interface, enum or record declarations may appear. Something else was found there.
class, interface, enum, or record expect.cause: One closing brace too many, which ends the class early and leaves the rest of the file outside it.

incompatible types.explanation: A value of one type was put where a different type is required. Java checks this before the program runs.
incompatible types.cause: Assigning text to a number variable, or forgetting to convert a value.
incompatible types.example:
int age = "12";                  // text into a number
int age = Integer.parseInt("12"); // convert first

missing return statement.explanation: A method promises to return a value, and there is a way to reach its end without returning one.
missing return statement.cause: A return inside an if with no return for the else path.

variable might not have been initialized.explanation: A local variable is being read before anything has been stored in it. Java refuses to guess a starting value.
variable might not have been initialized.cause: Declaring a variable and only assigning it inside an if that might not run.

unreachable statement.explanation: There is code that can never run, because the line before it always leaves the method or the loop.
unreachable statement.cause: A statement after return, break or continue.
unreachable statement.example:
return total;
System.out.println(total);   // can never run

method does not override or implement a.explanation: A method is marked @Override, but nothing in the parent class or interface has that exact signature to override.
method does not override or implement a.cause: A different spelling, a different number of parameters, or different parameter types from the method being overridden.

NullPointerException.explanation: Something used a dot on a variable holding null. null means "no object at all", so there is nothing to ask.
NullPointerException.cause: A variable that was never given an object, or a method that returned null when nothing was found.

ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.explanation: You asked for a position that does not exist in the array. An array of 3 has positions 0, 1 and 2.
ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.cause: Counting from 1 instead of 0, or a loop condition using <= where < was meant.

StringIndexOutOfBoundsException.explanation: You asked for a character at a position the string does not have.
StringIndexOutOfBoundsException.cause: charAt or substring with a position past the end - the last character is at length() - 1.

NumberFormatException.explanation: Text was converted to a number and the text was not a number.
NumberFormatException.cause: Integer.parseInt on input that contains letters, spaces or is empty.
NumberFormatException.example:
Integer.parseInt("12 ");    // the space is not a digit
Integer.parseInt("12 ".trim());

ArithmeticException.explanation: An impossible calculation was attempted - almost always dividing a whole number by zero.
ArithmeticException.cause: A count or a length that turned out to be 0.
ArithmeticException.example:
int average = total / count;   // count is 0
if (count != 0) average = total / count;

ClassCastException.explanation: An object was cast to a type it is not. The cast compiled, but at run time the object turned out to be something else.
ClassCastException.cause: Taking something out of a collection and assuming its type.

InputMismatchException.explanation: A Scanner was asked for one kind of value and the input held another.
InputMismatchException.cause: nextInt() when the person typed a word, or a leftover newline from a previous read.
InputMismatchException.example:
int age = scanner.nextInt();      // the input was "twelve"
String line = scanner.nextLine();  // read it as text and convert yourself

NoSuchElementException.explanation: Something was read from a source that has nothing left in it.
NoSuchElementException.cause: A Scanner reading past the end of the input, or next() on an iterator that is finished.

ConcurrentModificationException.explanation: A collection was changed while a for-each loop was walking through it. The loop cannot continue safely.
ConcurrentModificationException.cause: Calling add or remove on the list inside a loop over that same list.

StackOverflowError.explanation: A method called itself over and over until Java ran out of room to remember the calls.
StackOverflowError.cause: A recursive method whose stopping condition is missing or never reached.
StackOverflowError.example:
int count(int n) { return count(n - 1); }   // never stops
int countOk(int n) { return n <= 0 ? 0 : countOk(n - 1); }
